key_insight: ORSMT uses exact SMT checks to detect and repair semantic mismatches between LLM-generated optimization models and solver code, rather than relying on matching objective values.
engineering_relevance: It adds a verification layer to automated optimization workflows, checking that repairs preserve required feasible-region and objective relations.
method: Align observable decisions through a typed semantic interface and project out auxiliary variables.
Prove or refute semantic relations with SMT queries, localizing failures to implicated constraints or domains.
Reconstruct artifacts and adopt candidates only after required relation checks pass.
evidence_signal: Across 3,034 problems and six generator sizes, protected selection increased aggregate model-code matching from 43.2% to 88.2%, while correct-and-matched outputs rose from 25.2% to 40.2%.
watch_item: Model-code agreement does not guarantee source correctness: both artifacts can omit the same requirement, so source-grounded validation remains necessary.
paper_title: ORSMT: Unleashing the Potential of Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Semantic Verification and Repair in LLM-Based Optimization
